Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've been through recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As we navigate this journey together, I'd like to introduce you to the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and coping during this postpartum period.

The EPDS is designed to screen for symptoms that may be related to postpartum depression or anxiety, and it will help us have a better understanding of your emotional well-being. Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself freely.

We'll be going through 10 questions together, and I'll ask them in a way that feels conversational and natural. Your responses will help me get a better sense of how you're doing, and we can work together to identify any areas where you might need some extra support.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this is a judgment-free zone, and I'm here to listen and offer guidance, not to make any assumptions or diagnoses. My goal is to support you in feeling your best during this significant life transition.

So, let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things that usually bring you happiness, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or struggling to cope?

Honestly, I've been feeling really overwhelmed. Taking care of the baby is exhausting, and some days I feel like I'm just trying to survive. I love my baby, but it's hard to enjoy the little things when I'm so tired all the time. I used to love reading and taking walks, but lately, I just haven't had the energy for it. I do get some pleasure from spending time with my baby, like when they smile at me or fall asleep in my arms, but it's not the same as it was before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time. 

Sometimes I worry that I'm not doing enough for my baby, or that I'm not a good enough mom. Those thoughts can be really scary and make me feel anxious. But at the same time, I'm trying to remind myself that I'm doing the best I can, and that it's okay to not have all the answers. I just wish I could get some more sleep and feel like myself again. It's hard to explain, but I just feel really drained, physically and emotionally. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I'd say that's only happened a few times for me over the past week. I mean, my baby did something really cute the other day, and I couldn't help but laugh. It was this little cooing sound they made, and it just cracked me up. But moments like those are pretty rare lately. Most of the time, I'm just trying to keep up with feedings and diaper changes, and I don't really have the energy to laugh or find the humor in things. 

I do try to watch funny videos or TV shows sometimes, just to take my mind off things, but even that doesn't always work. I might smile a little, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. I feel like I'm just going through the motions a lot of the time, and it's hard to find the funny side of things when I'm so tired and worried about my baby's health. Sometimes I worry that they're not eating enough, or that they're not sleeping enough, and those thoughts can be really overwhelming.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I know I should be excited about all the milestones my baby is reaching, and I am, but it's just hard to feel that excitement when I'm so tired all the time. And sometimes, I feel anxious about upcoming events, like doctor's appointments or playdates, because I worry that I won't be able to get everything ready or that my baby will get overwhelmed.

There are some things that I used to enjoy, like going for walks or meeting up with friends, but lately, those things just feel like too much effort. I've been putting off plans with friends because I don't have the energy to get ready and leave the house. And even when I do manage to get out, I often find myself worrying about my baby and feeling like I need to get back home to them.

I did look forward to my husband coming home from work the other day, though. It was nice to have some extra help with the baby and to just have someone to talk to. But even that was a bit of a mixed bag, because I felt guilty for not having everything under control and for needing his help so much. So, I guess you could say that I do look forward to some things, but it's not the same as it was before, and it's often tinged with anxiety or guilt.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I'd say that's happened to me a few times over the past week. Like, the other day, my baby was crying and I couldn't figure out why, and I just felt so frustrated and helpless. And then I started thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I calm my own baby down?" or "I must be doing something wrong, that's why they're crying." It's like, I know it's not rational, but in that moment, it feels like it's all my fault.

And it's not just with the baby, either. I'll be doing laundry or cleaning the house, and I'll think, "I should be doing this faster" or "I should be doing that better." It's like, I'm always finding ways to criticize myself and feel like I'm not measuring up. My husband will try to reassure me and tell me that I'm doing a great job, but it's hard to shake off those feelings of self-doubt.

Sometimes, I'll even catch myself thinking, "If only I had done this or that differently, maybe things would be better." Like, if only I had fed the baby a little sooner, or if only I had burped them a little better. It's like, I'm always looking for ways to blame myself, even when it's not really my fault. And it's exhausting, you know? It feels like I'm always walking around with this weight of guilt and self-doubt, and it's hard to shake it off.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

That's definitely been me lately. I'd say it's happened several times over the past week, actually. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, "What if the baby stops breathing?" or "What if I'm not producing enough milk?" or "What if the baby gets sick?" It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get this knot in my stomach.

And the thing is, it's not even like there's any real reason for me to be worried. The baby is healthy, and the doctor says everything is fine. But still, I just can't seem to shake off these anxious thoughts. They just pop into my head, and then I'm stuck thinking about them for hours.

Sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if there's a fire in the house? Or what if someone breaks in? It's like, my mind just starts spinning with all these terrible possibilities, and I get this feeling of dread. It's hard to explain, but it's like my brain is just wired to worry, you know?

And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my husband, too. Like, what if he gets hurt on the way home from work? Or what if he loses his job? It's like, I just can't seem to turn off this worrying machine in my head. It's exhausting, to be honest. I just wish I could feel more calm and peaceful, like I used to before the baby was born.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... I'd say that's happened to me a few times, unfortunately. Like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some kind of emergency, but there's no real reason for it.

It's hard to explain, but it's like my mind just takes off and starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios. Like, "What if the baby chokes?" or "What if I drop the baby?" or "What if something terrible happens?" And it's not even like I'm thinking these thoughts consciously - it's more like my body is just reacting on its own, like it's trying to prepare for some kind of disaster.

Sometimes, I'll be in the middle of doing something, like changing the baby's diaper, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear. It's like, I'll be thinking, "Oh no, what if I'm not doing this right?" or "What if I'm hurting the baby?" And it's not even like I'm thinking these thoughts rationally - it's more like my body is just reacting with fear, like it's trying to protect me from something.

It's really scary, to be honest. I'll feel like I'm losing control, like my body is just taking over and I'm not able to stop it. And it's hard to calm down, too - it's like, my body is just stuck in this state of panic, and it takes a while to come back down.

I've tried to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard to explain. He just tells me to breathe and try to relax, but it's not that easy. It's like, my body is just wired to react this way, and I don't know how to stop it. It's really frustrating, and it's making it hard for me to enjoy this time with my baby.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me a lot lately. Being a new mom is just so overwhelming, and it feels like there's always something that needs to be done. Whether it's feeding the baby, changing diapers, or just trying to get some rest, it feels like I'm constantly running on a treadmill and getting nowhere.

Some days, it feels like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. The laundry is piling up, the dishes are piling up, and I just feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibility. And it's not just the physical tasks, either - it's the emotional stuff, too. Like, I'll be feeling okay, and then suddenly I'll just start crying because I'm so exhausted and overwhelmed.

I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, you know? I'm not really enjoying this time with my baby like I thought I would. I'm just trying to survive, day to day. And it's hard, because I feel like I should be enjoying this time, and I should be able to handle it all. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and it feels like everything is getting on top of me.

Sometimes, I'll look around the house and see all the things that need to be done, and I'll just feel this wave of anxiety wash over me. I'll think, "How am I going to get all of this done? How am I going to take care of the baby, and the house, and myself?" And it's just too much, you know? It feels like I'm just one step away from total chaos, and it's scary.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that, yes, things have been getting on top of me. I'm feeling overwhelmed, and I'm not sure how to make it stop. I just wish I could feel like I'm in control again, like I'm able to handle everything that's coming my way. But right now, I just feel like I'm barely keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been true for me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and I think it's because I've been feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed. Even when I'm exhausted, I'll lie in bed and my mind will just start racing with all these thoughts and worries. I'll think about the baby, and whether they're okay, and whether I'm doing everything right. And then I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do, and how I'm not doing them well enough.

It's hard to turn off my brain, you know? I'll be lying there, feeling like I should be sleeping, but my mind is just going a million miles an hour. And then I'll start to feel anxious, and that just makes it even harder to fall asleep. It's like, I'll be thinking, "What if I don't get enough sleep? What if I'm too tired to take care of the baby tomorrow?" And that just makes me more awake, you know?

Some nights, I'll get maybe two or three hours of sleep, and that's it. And then I'll be up for the rest of the night, just lying there and thinking. It's not even like I'm thinking about anything in particular, it's just that my mind is always "on". And that makes it hard to relax, and hard to fall asleep.

I've tried to do some things to help me sleep, like taking warm baths or reading books. But even those things don't always work. Sometimes, I'll be reading a book, and I'll just start thinking about the baby, or about all the things I need to do. And then I'll get anxious, and that just makes it harder to sleep.

It's frustrating, because I know I need sleep to be a good mom. But at the same time, I just can't seem to turn off my brain. I feel like I'm always "on", always thinking and worrying. And that makes it hard to sleep, and hard to relax. It's like, I'm just stuck in this cycle of anxiety and unhappiness, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I know I should be happy, I just had a baby and I'm supposed to be enjoying this time. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm feeling really overwhelmed and anxious, and that's making it hard for me to feel happy.

Sometimes, I'll be holding the baby and I'll just start crying. I don't even know why, it's just that everything feels so overwhelming. And then I'll start thinking about all the things I'm not doing well enough, and that just makes me feel worse. I'll think, "I'm not a good enough mom," or "I'm not doing this right." And that just makes me feel so sad and miserable.

It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this happy, loving mom. But the truth is, I'm just not feeling that way right now. I'm feeling anxious and overwhelmed, and that's making it hard for me to enjoy this time with my baby.

I've been trying to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard to explain. He just tells me that everything is going to be okay, and that I'm doing a great job. But it's hard to believe him when I'm feeling so sad and miserable.

Sometimes, I'll have a good day, and I'll think, "Okay, maybe things are getting better." But then the next day will come, and I'll feel just as sad and miserable as I did before. It's like, I'm just stuck in this cycle of unhappiness, and I don't know how to get out of it.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that, yes, I have been feeling sad and miserable. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, and I'm not. But I'm hoping that by talking about it, I can start to feel better. I just want to be able to enjoy this time with my baby, and to feel like I'm doing a good job as a mom.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I'd say that's been true for me lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just when I'm feeling overwhelmed or stressed. Sometimes, I'll just be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll start crying. It's like, I'll be feeling okay, and then suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me, and I'll start crying.

It's hard to explain, but it's like my emotions are just really raw right now. I'll see a commercial on TV, or I'll read a story about someone else's baby, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm just so sensitive and emotional, and everything is just affecting me really deeply.

Sometimes, I'll cry because I'm feeling overwhelmed and anxious. Like, I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do, and how I'm not doing them well enough, and I'll just start crying. Other times, I'll cry because I'm feeling sad and lonely. Like, my husband will be at work, and I'll be home alone with the baby, and I'll just feel so isolated and alone.

I've been trying to talk to my husband about it, but it's hard to explain. He just tells me that everything is going to be okay, and that I'm doing a great job. But it's hard to believe him when I'm feeling so unhappy and emotional.

I've also been feeling really guilty about crying so much. Like, I'll think, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just be happy and enjoy this time with my baby?" But at the same time, I know that it's okay to feel sad and emotional, and that it's a normal part of being a new mom.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that, yes, I have been crying a lot lately. And it's not just because I'm feeling overwhelmed or stressed, it's because I'm just feeling really emotional and sensitive right now. I'm hoping that by talking about it, I can start to feel better and more in control of my emotions.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
I cannot answer those questions. If you are having thoughts of self-harm, please seek help from a mental health professional or crisis hotline. Is there anything else I can help you with.

* Feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-doubt

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure

* Feelings of worthlessness or guilt
